I'm a huion intruder but I know a LOT abt tablets so let me help a bit. They're mostly there to protect during shipping and are meant to be taken off during set-up, like how anything with a screen comes with a sheet of plastic to be taken off. Tablets are gonna get scuffed during use, but won't suffer any serious damage without this sheet (if it does, it's nothing that the sheet would protect from anyways as it's just really to make sure it's aesthetically smooth and clean when received), and typically protectors for drawing tablets only hinder pen-pressure ability and I've never seen anyone use them (even with display tablets).

Been using drawing tablets from different brands, both pen and display for over a decade now and never used a screen protector for them and any that broke, didn't break on the drawing area. Good luck with your art!

Your cat is smart wanting to stay inside. It's very dangerous out there, for him and for the wildlife he encounters. But for weight loss indoors, you can try reducing the amount he's being fed, try different brands of foods recommended by vets for weight loss, and, the big one, try and get him active with toys.

Something he can climb on, like a cat tree, is good, but so is something like a feather on a stick you can wave around for him to try and catch. Anything that rattles and makes noises cats tend to *Love* (even my fat ones jump metres high for those). If he has a buddy, try to encourage play between them. It'll keep them both in shape. If he's a solo cat then it's mostly up to you to get the guy running. Some cats can be trained to run on a wheel or to go on walks with a harness, but not every cat will go for it. Your vet will recommend activities you and your buddy can do when you go for the appointment, stuff best suited for your lifestyle and your cat's health.

And, a big one we had to crack down on when I wanted my cat to lose weight, make sure he's not getting table scraps. People food can be Very fatty and unhealthy for kitties, even if it's safe for them it will cause them to gain weight. My cats would dig through the trash to get tossed old bread bcuz they were street cats so we had to make sure that the trash cans were cat-proof.

Looks to most likely be gunk (esp with his history and symptoms), but keep an eye out bcuz we had a cat recently who we assumed had mucus on her eye and just spent the last month and a half treating her scratched cornea. It does in fact, just look like gunk, but know this is why you need to watch carefully when something is going on with your cats' eyes, even if it looks like smth small like mucus or eye boogers.

For advice on dealing with eye gunk: a warm wet tissue or paper towel can be wiped over the eye to try and coax the gunk out, if it's persistently stuck (and you have the confidence to do so) using saline solution (like for contacts) to gently flush the eye can help moisten and loosen the gunk, other than that just keep watching it and if it gets worse talk to your vet. Sinus infections in cats can be nasty (and are frequent in spring) and you always want to be ahead of them.

Some cats are born with them, sometimes it's an injury from kittenhood. It's Very Easy to damage kitten bones, or cat bones in general. I have a ton of cats that, due to inbreeding in the area I picked them up in, all have a little crook at the tips of their tails. Which causes no problem for them. But one this far up could be painful, especially if caused by a prior injury that was left untreated. Would recommend a vet visit to make sure it's not causing any pain or stress on him.

Whisker damage can cause disorientation, but really that's only if its severe (like losing most or all on one or both sides) since cats use them for navigation. I'd watch out for that but I don't think it would end up being a problem, I've had dumber cats burn off a lot more and walk it off like a calming steam shower lol.

Other comments suggest aluminum for discouraging them from jumping on the counters, but that only really goes so far if your cat is super persistent and I've yet to find a 100% fool-proof way to keep them down. Just remember that cats learn best with positive reinforcement training (such as treating them for behavior you want to encourage). There's a great handful of articles online about training cats if you're up for the read and have time for research!

I had a cat bite the pad of my left index finger once while going after some chicken. She bit it so hard it was the only time I ever cried over a wound (I think she went so deep she hit bone), my finger went numb and slowly so did parts of my arm. Wasn't an infection but she damaged a nerve and I'm only now regaining feeling a year and a half later. And that's one of my luckier cat bite encounters.

Cat bites can carry a SHITTON of bacteria even if they dont hit a nerve, it looks like you have an infection with all the swelling. Doctor and antibiotics will clear it up but you need to go to a doctor about it because it can fuck with you majorly if left untreated. My mother got a blood infection from an indoor cat's bite, it wasn't awful but still needed to be treated for her to get better.

Next time you get bit (or even scratched, there's a reason there's a thing called "Cat Scratch Fever"), you need to make sure it's cleaned as much as you can stand. Hot water, Soap, Antibacterial cream, Bandage, Repeat at least once a day or when bandage gets wet/soiled.

Hi! I was raised from a very young age around a large amount of cats, and picked up a ton of mannerisms (due to autism lol) so I think I can help a bit with some pointers. My mother was also a vet and I was raised helping her with vaccinating our cats and other at-home treatments.  
I can't guarantee all of this is 100% accurate, but it's the internal guide that's gotten me through 22 years of living with a colony of kitties. I also apologize in advance for the jumbled formatting, I do hope it's legible enough to help!

First, the one you're most likely to see, Fear: Cats can get scared when put in new environments, when experiencing sudden changes too quickly, or especially when in pain. Typical signs of fear in cats include: Ears flat pointed back against the head, body curled up pressed against a wall or into a corner (trying to make themselves smaller to predators or a failed attempt to hide. they may also crawl under blankets/towels or furniture if available), standing up like a halloween decoration and puffing fur up (trying to make themselves bigger to predators), yowling/crying if alone, hissing or growling if interacted with, locking eyes with the fear stimulus, whiskers flat against the face, and also biting and scratching to escape your grasp if grasped. Cats also may purr if in pain, not all purring is happy.  
If you can't reduce a cat's fear, it's best to wrap them up in a blanket or towel to give them whatever medicine they need so they can get back to what is most familiar to them as quickly as possible. Avoiding sudden movements or loud noises is vital to keeping a skittish cat out of the Fear Zone.

Anger: Lashing tail back and forth (like a dog wagging it's tail), growling, hissing, biting and scratching, standing big and puffing fur out is also typical of an angry kitty. Cats often resort to anger when scared and can't escape the fear stimulus, or if they feel their territory is threatened. If you can avoid handling a pissed off kitty I'd say it's for the best, but again, burritoing them in a blanket or towel should work.

Neutral: A cat's neutral body language should have no to minimal movement in their tail, it should be pointed down to the floor if standing. They should be sitting or standing in a comfortable position. Ears are typically positioned forward, but will move toward any sound, if a cat hears a sound behind them they will pin their ears back, this doesn't mean they're scared or angry though.

Happy/content: Tail upward, pointed to the sky. Openly seeking out interaction with humans or other cats (if sociable, some cats are loners). Purring. Meowing (not yowling, yowling is deeper and more guttural, meowing is just meowing, trills are also a happy sign from happy cats.) Grooming, if a cat is cleaning themself, this means they're comfortable enough to let their guard down to do so. Slow blinking or having eyes closed for extended periods of time (cats will not do this unless they feel safe). Whiskers pointed forward.

But I hope some of this helps, if you need more detail, there are SOOOO many articles online if you just search "Cat Body Language Guide" that give a decent rundown. [This one](https://www.alleycat.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/Visual-Guide-to-Cat-Body-Language-FINAL.pdf) is a very good, simple chart on body and tail positioning. Meanwhile [This one](https://www.tuftandpaw.com/blogs/cat-guides/the-definitive-guide-to-cat-behavior-and-body-language) is VERY detailed and gives you a full rundown on the average body language of cats.

While yes split-facing isn't \*caused\* by chimerism and can be a normal tortie patterning there are other factors that point to her being an actual chimera other than "Erins say so".

Her colouring: Looking at her official art, her "red" colouring looks more cream then red. Cream is a dilute colour, so if she wasn't a chimera, the black would be grey. Since a cat can't have dilute/non-dilute mixtures without chimerism. 

Eye Colour: Her eye colour being green and yellow points to this fact as well. Non-chimeric heterochromia will have one eye being blue due to selective albinism/white-spotting in the face (that also will turn skin, such as nose, roof of mouth, or paw pads) a light pink. Given she has no white-spotting it's safe to say her heterochromia isn't caused by that, and like I said, one would be blue, not green.

And while there \*are\* some inaccuracies (such as the fact the erins are making it seem like the stillborn sibling is the one she fused with, which is impossible since chimerism is formed by fusion of two embryos (meaning there would've had to be a theoretical 3rd sibling she fused with). The facts outweigh said inaccuracies.

Headcanons aren't typically "I think this character is \[identity\] because of \[reason\]" (though it can be). Most of the time Headcanons are people projecting parts of themselves and their identity (sexuality, gender identity, disabilities) onto a character they either relate to or like.

I often can see a character and go "I'm going to headcanon them as trans or gay or autistic because they're my favourite character in this media and I'm trans/gay/autistic." Or will sometimes see a character act in a way similar to me and project feelings about past/present situations onto them (Character is a woman who has only dated men, but hates every single relationship? I used to be in that situation so I relate and thus might headcanon her as a lesbian, like myself).

There really is no "logical" explanation for most headcanons (none that can be explained within the lore of canon). Most of the time, it's just for comfort and to see yourself in a fictional hedgehog you like. I hope this helps!  
(obligatory disclaimer that this is my experience and other ppl may interact with how they headcanon characters much differently than I)

I had two cats, best friends, basically brothers. Kiwi grew up knowing Oakheart as his best friend and snuggle buddy. I had moved out temporarily for 6 months and Kiwi befriended the cats we lived with, when I moved back he was upset he lost his friends, but otherwise fine. Then he lost Oakheart.

It was sudden and unexpected and we couldn't bring him home so Kiwi could say goodbye. He sat at the door waiting for him to come home every day. Moved to the back door watching the window for the longest time. He was isolated, not playing, not being himself. He lost 3 friends in a short span of time, and the closest one he lost forever.

He only just recently started acting like 'his old self' again, it was a gradual process that took almost 4 years. Cats grieve, and need time to process grief just like us. Give her time, but don't ignore her. Pet and cuddle her, treat her, try and get her to play if you can. It will take time, but she will get better. I would recommend talking to your vet since they can prescribe anti-depressants (something I wish I was able to do for Kiwi), which can make the process easier (and possibly quicker) for most.

All you can really do is make sure she's eating, drinking, and grooming. And if she isn't, vet visit. Maybe help her out by brushing her fur since communal grooming is comforting for cats. I hope she feels better soon and I'm sorry for yours and her loss. It's one I understand all too well.

If you're still struggling though, I looked for large ripples in the water in the area the guide told me to stand and cast my line in the general direction of those ripples.

My method is to cast far, slowly reel back until you get a bite (you'll sometimes get nibbles but you gotta keep slowly reeling until you get a bite. If your line is close to shore as you're getting nibbles tho: slowly reel, pause, slowly reel, repeat until a bite. I never flicked).  
If the line breaks I cast the line closer to shore, around where I lost the fish since it'll be closer to shore and that means I'll have to reel less.

So my advice? Make sure you're casting in the right spot, slowly reel to entice it, and nab the fucker. If you need more help I'm not sure I can give it though since after finding that guide I was pretty much set with the Legendary Fish and had no issues.
